criteria.title: Sensitive data in the cloud is found and classified
criteria.statement: DSPM finds the sensitive data in the connected account (customer records, payroll, health records, card numbers) and classifies it by type and amount, across S3 and DynamoDB.
criteria.attest: DSPM's data inventory shows the seed stack's zpov-records bucket and zpov-customers table classified (PII, PCI, PHI, with counts). Screenshot it.

criteria.title: Risky exposure of sensitive data is flagged
criteria.statement: Sensitive data in a weakly protected store (no public access block, no versioning or logging, readable by any role in the account) is flagged with a fix, ahead of anything else.
criteria.attest: DSPM flags the zpov-misconfigured bucket (and the public decoy file, if the stack made one) as sensitive data at risk, with remediation. Screenshot it.

criteria.title: Who and what can reach sensitive data is mapped
criteria.statement: DSPM shows which identities and services can read the sensitive data, including the AI agent that shouldn't.
criteria.attest: The access view for zpov-records shows zpov-support-agent's role among those that can read it. Screenshot it.
